name: Nardil + Vorinostat social-confidence stack

lead: On looksmax.org, users describe combining Nardil (phenelzine), an older prescription antidepressant, with vorinostat (Zolinza), an approved cutaneous T-cell lymphoma drug, as a way to become less inhibited, calmer and more talkative in social settings. The looks angle is about presence: confident body language, eye contact and ease are treated as part of how a person comes across.

Posters report effects such as reduced social anxiety, a feeling they call hypomania, and an easier time approaching people. No published trial has tested the pairing, and vorinostat is not approved for any psychiatric use; individual accounts are anecdotal.

paras: Descriptions are anecdotal: users say they obtain phenelzine from a psychiatrist, report an initial adjustment period of days to weeks, and add vorinostat later, sometimes alongside other drugs such as caffeine or a beta blocker. Forum threads also discuss difficulty getting a prescription. This wiki does not give doses or sourcing.

Phenelzine is an irreversible MAOI; labelling and reference sources describe dietary tyramine restrictions and dangerous interactions with serotonergic drugs, stimulants and some opioids, plus risks of mania, liver injury and low blood pressure.[1] Vorinostat is a chemotherapy-class drug with poor brain penetrance in animals.[2] Posters themselves mention constipation and warn against use after a manic episode.

angle.text: Users say the stack makes them more talkative and less anxious, which they connect with coming across as more charismatic. These are self-reports, and the combination has not been studied.

lead: The Nardil + vorinostat stack is a pairing discussed on looksmax.org in which users combine phenelzine (brand Nardil), a prescription monoamine oxidase inhibitor, with vorinostat, a histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitor approved for cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. Posters present it as a route to being low-inhibition and socially at ease, which they treat as part of ascending.[1][2]

Phenelzine is an irreversible, non-selective MAOI used for depression and anxiety disorders, including treatment-resistant depression; it requires attention to tyramine-rich foods and interacting drugs.[3] Vorinostat was the first HDAC inhibitor approved by the FDA, in 2006 for cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.[4] A thread titled as a 'social god mode' stack adds the anticonvulsant pregabalin (Lyrica) and caffeine, and its author describes inducing hypomania as the aim.[2]
The forum accounts are individual reports. No clinical trial has examined phenelzine and vorinostat together for social confidence.
infobox: Prescription-only in the US and Australia[3]

paras: Phenelzine has been described since a 1932 synthesis and is used for major depression, atypical depression and anxiety disorders such as social anxiety and panic disorder.[3] Vorinostat is a 100 mg oral capsule drug for lymphoma that works by blocking HDAC enzymes.[4]

One poster calls Nardil 'hypomania in a pill' and says it improves energy and motivation, and also describes needing a physician willing to prescribe it.[1] Another writes that the three-drug stack left them 'low inhib' and socially fluent but constipated.[2] Posts describe a honeymoon phase early in treatment which some hope vorinostat will extend.[1]
The reasoning described is that disinhibition removes the social hesitation that users associate with being seen as less attractive.

Reference sources list orthostatic hypotension, insomnia, weight gain, sexual dysfunction and, rarely, mania and liver failure as phenelzine adverse effects, and warn about serotonin toxicity with SSRIs, MDMA and some opioids and about stimulants such as amphetamines.[3] Forum posters note that many recreational drugs cannot be combined with it and that anyone with prior mania should avoid it.[1]
In animal work vorinostat produced only subtle brain HDAC inhibition and is pumped out by efflux transporters.[4]

No studies found. Phenelzine has been studied for social anxiety and other disorders as a single agent,[3] and vorinostat has been trialled in cancers and studied for Niemann-Pick type C1,[4] but the combination for social confidence has not been tested.

lore.intro: Threads on looksmax.org present the pairing as a pharmacological shortcut to social ease; most replies are short endorsements or requests for prescribing advice.[1][2]
